text:
alex_m: Heads-up — Support flagged multiple customers asking why a request landed on a lower-cost fallback model instead of the preferred model. They want a per-request explanation + a quick units estimate they can display in the app. Idea: add an opt-in debug header that returns routing decision + estimated embed-units + a trace id. Thoughts?

priya: yes please. we already have routing info in traces but it's not surfaced to API clients. opt-in header sounds good, but we need sampling + scrub sensitive bits.

jin: propose a tiny header API: `X-Redwood-Debug: route,units,trace` — server returns lightweight headers like:
```
X-Redwood-Route: model=redwood-v2-emb, tier=dedicated, shard=3
X-Redwood-Units: 12
X-Redwood-Trace: r-6b23e...
```
Keep body unchanged to avoid breaking clients. The header values are short and cheap to compute (approx estimator).

sam_k: +1 for header approach. concern: computing an "estimated units" could be expensive if we run full preflight for every request. Can we reuse the fast preflight estimator (the one used by the console preflight) with a "fast" mode? That should be O(1) heuristics.

priya: agreed — use the existing preflight estimator in fast mode. Also: MUST be opt-in per-request (debug header) and tenant-level sampling to avoid noise. default sample-rate 10% for debug header to limit cost.

alex_m: Console UX note: customers want a human-readable "Why this route?" panel on the request detail page that shows the header and a simple decision tree (e.g., capacity->latency_sla->fallback). We can link the header trace id to a read-only explain endpoint in the console.

jin: console plan: add a small "Routing trace (debug)" link that calls `/internal/route-explain?trace_id=<id>` and returns sanitized steps. Endpoint MUST strip prompt/token contents and only return decision metadata. This endpoint should be RBAC-protected.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: routing-debug-header v1 -> 10% on staging at 2024-11-02T04:00Z :rocket:

sam_k: security check — make sure we don't leak tenant billing-sensitive data to other tenants or to public logs. `X-Redwood-Units` should only be returned to the request originator; support staff can view richer traces via console with tenant consent. Add unit tests to assert headers are tenant-scoped.

priya: telemetry: emit a `routing.debug.request` event with fields: `route_variant`, `est_units_bucket` (0-4), `sample_rate`. No PII. Global sample 1% for metrics, 100% for tenant-debug sessions (when tenant opts in).

alex_m: quick UX constraints: 
- header must be short (<128 chars)
- estimator error budget: ±20% OK for UI display
- default sampling: 10% for header, 1% for telemetry

jin: i'll prototype the header PR. rough sketch for server side:
```go
// pseudo
if req.Header.Get("X-Redwood-Debug") != "" && in_sample(req.tenant) {
  route := computeRoutingDecisionFast(req)
  est := fastUnitEstimator(req.payload_shape)
  w.Header().Set("X-Redwood-Route", route.Short())
  w.Header().Set("X-Redwood-Units", strconv.Itoa(est))
  w.Header().Set("X-Redwood-Trace", route.TraceID)
}
```

sam_k: add a security flag to the header logic to ensure only authorized internal agents can request full explain (console). Also add a rate-limit for debug headers per tenant to avoid abuse.

priya: i'll mock the console panel after standup and scope RBAC. cc @alex_m :thumbsup:

alex_m: action items:
- jin: implement header + fast estimator (PR + unit tests)
- priya: console panel + RBAC mockups + telemetry schema
- sam_k: threat model + tests for tenant isolation + rate-limits
- ops: coordinate canary rollout and SLO measurement

priya: filing follow-up RFC and will link design mock in the thread. thanks everyone!
